entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ernest II of Saxony (1450–1513) was a pivotal figure in the complex web of alliances and conflicts that defined the late medieval era of Western Europe.

As Archbishop of Magdeburg and Administrator of the Diocese of Halberstadt, Ernest II played a crucial role in shaping the ecclesiastical landscape of the Holy Roman Empire. His leadership during the tumultuous years of the 15th century, marked by the Black Death, the Hundred Years' War, and the rise of Protestantism, had far-reaching consequences for the religious and political dynamics of the region.

Ernest II's significance extends beyond his individual accomplishments, as he embodied the tensions between the power of the Church and the growing influence of secular rulers. His legacy, though often overshadowed by the more famous figures of the era, contributes to our understanding of the complex interplay between religious and political institutions during the medieval period.

The 1513 death of Ernest II of Saxony marked the end of an era, as the fragile balance of power in Western Europe was forever altered by the rise of Protestantism and the decline of the Holy Roman Empire.
